messages:
maria: Quick sync — we need to decide how to handle token refill jitter for token-bucket enforcement. We're seeing correlated bursts when many clients refill at the same time.
ajay: Yep. Seen in staging. Those synchronized refills cause transient 429 spikes even though steady-state is fine.
kevin: Two knobs that help: add jitter to the refill schedule; and add a leaky/decay layer for org-level smoothing. Token bucket for short bursts, leaky bucket for long-run rate.
leah: Here's a config sketch I've been testing locally: 

```
policy: {
  type: "token_bucket",
  capacity: 500,
  refill_tokens: 50,
  refill_interval_ms: 1000,
  refill_jitter_ms: 300,
  burst_decay_ms: 15000,
  fallback_policy: "queue_or_429"
}
```

Jitter prevents alignment across clients. burst_decay is used to simulate a leaky drain on the effective credits.
ajay: That looks good. We should decide scope: per-key default, per-org override for enterprise? Per-key is fair to clients, but if an org has many keys it can still hammer the infra.
maria: I like hierarchical enforcement: per-key token buckets + per-org leaky bucket. That allows single clients to burst but prevents aggregate saturation.
kevin: Agree. Implementation note: per-key buckets are cheap and sharded; org-level leaky bucket can be approximate (count-min or a small token reservoir) to reduce state. Also add a short-term high-water mark to detect collision spikes.
leah: Telemetry we need to surface: 1) 429 rate by key/org 2) token refill collisions (concurrent refills/sec) 3) queue length and avg wait 4) p50/p95 latency before/after throttling 5) credits_remaining over time.
ajay: Dashboards: compact per-org card showing effective throughput, credits_left, time_to_recover (if abused), and recent 429 spikes. Add alert rule: sustained 429 rate + rising queue length -> auto rollback.
maria: For Console UX: product wants a preview slider so customers can simulate raising burst capacity and see estimated cost + latency impact. Also show 'effective limit' computed from hierarchical policy.
sre-oncall: Rollout safety: enable high-verbosity logging behind a flag in staging and canary. Also a circuit-breaker that auto-reverts policy for an org if 429s exceed threshold.
deploy-bot: applied policy change to staging (policy-refill-jitter-v1) — rollout started.
kevin: Proposed rollout: feature-flagged code path in staging -> 5% canary across low-traffic orgs -> 25% -> 100% with 30m observation windows. Automated rollback triggers: 3x baseline 429s or org queue > 50 for 10m.
leah: Also define SLO for burst handling: "For bursts <= 1k tokens within 10s, 99% of requests should not be 429". We can refine after data.
maria: Action items: leah to add telemetry panels and alerts; kevin to implement hierarchical leaky layer + collision metric; ajay to build test harness to simulate many keys refilling simultaneously; I'll write rollout doc and own the feature flag.
leah: Will add dashboards by EOD tomorrow and wire alerts.
ajay: I'll share the load-simulator infra and a small script to spike 10k keys at once.
maria: Perfect. Thanks all :thumbsup: If anyone hits edge cases while testing drop me a DM.
